root_cause.text: The `handshake_req_cancel()` function in `net/handshake/request.c` fails to set the `HANDSHAKE_F_REQ_COMPLETED` flag in `req->hr_flags` when a pending handshake request is first cancelled, allowing a subsequent duplicate cancellation request to bypass the completion check and release the socket reference again.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff adds `test_and_set_bit(HANDSHAKE_F_REQ_COMPLETED, &req->hr_flags)` to the `remove_pending()` block in `handshake_req_cancel()`. The commit message explains that if a second cancellation request arrives, `remove_pending()` returns false, and because `HANDSHAKE_F_REQ_COMPLETED` is not set, the code continues to the `out_true` label, causing a duplicate socket reference release and a refcount underflow.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a race condition in handshake cancellation by atomically marking the pending request as completed during removal.
intent_record.what: Added a test_and_set_bit check for HANDSHAKE_F_REQ_COMPLETED and a trace call within the pending request removal block of handshake_req_cancel.
intent_record.how: Prevents a race condition by ensuring that a pending request being cancelled is atomically marked as completed, returning false if it was already marked.

net/handshake: Create a NETLINK service for handling handshake requests

When a kernel consumer needs a transport layer
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 3b3009ea8abb713b022d94fba95ec270cf6e7eae
Author: Chuck Lever <chuck.lever@oracle.com>
Date:   Mon Apr 17 10:32:26 2023 -0400

    net/handshake: Create a NETLINK service for handling handshake requests
    
    When a kernel consumer needs a transport layer security session, it
    first needs a handshake to negotiate and establish a session. This
    negotiation can be done in user space via one of the several
    existing library implementations, or it can be done in the kernel.
bic_trace_step.reason: In handshake_req_cancel(), when a pending request is cancelled, the code executes 'if (hn && remove_pending(hn, req)) { goto out_true; }' (lines 317-320). This jumps directly to 'out_true' and calls 'sock_put(sk)' without setting the HANDSHAKE_F_REQ_COMPLETED flag in req->hr_flags. Consequently, a subsequent cancellation request for the same socket will find that remove_pending() returns false, and then test_and_set_bit(HANDSHAKE_F_REQ_COMPLETED, &req->hr_flags) will also return false (since the flag was never set), leading to a second 'sock_put(sk)' and a socket reference count underflow.

bic_trace_step.reason: In the function `handshake_req_cancel()`, if `remove_pending(hn, req)` is true, the code executes `goto out_true;` (lines 323-326). This bypasses the `test_and_set_bit(HANDSHAKE_F_REQ_COMPLETED, &req->hr_flags)` check on line 327. As a result, the `HANDSHAKE_F_REQ_COMPLETED` flag is never set when a pending request is cancelled. A subsequent call to `handshake_req_cancel()` will find that `remove_pending()` is false, but since the flag was not set, `test_and_set_bit()` will also return false, leading to a second `sock_put(sk)` on line 335, causing a socket reference count underflow.
